newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt rises on U.S. investor yield craving.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt rises on U.S. investor yield craving.

text.p: Emerging debt prices rose Tuesday as U.S. institutional investors pressed on in their quest for higher yields, Brady bond traders said.

"The buying we have seen has been mostly clients," said the chief Brady bond trader at a major U.S. bank. "There has not been one specific theme that driving the market up at this stage except that some moeny is being put to work."
Following the stable outcome of Mexico's Sunday elections, U.S. investors seemed more inclined to look to emerging market assets for value.

"You have a lot of inflows coming in because they basically don't see anything that is going to derail the performance we've had so far," said Joyce Chang, emerging markets debt strategist at Merrill Lynch.

Chang added that, despite a strong Brady bond rally and historically tight spreads against U.S. Treasuries, U.S. investors could still find higher yields in the emerging markets than in other asset markets.
Brady bonds surged despite a slipping U.S. bond market, where the benchmark U.S. T-bond lost 2/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
Argentine paper led the market higher, on continued optimism over comments by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez on Monday that Argentina would consider buying back some of its Brady bonds.
Argentine Discounts AR4C23=RR gained 1-1/4 to 88-3/4, while the country's Pars picked up 3/4 to 73.
The most liquid Brady assets trailed the market. Argentina's FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 1/4 to 95, and the Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR were up 1/4 tp 83.
"It's simply a change from short duration assets into longer duration assets, something that you are porbably seeing in the U.S. as well," one Brady dealer said.
